cards.explanation: The answer is until no place is left. Isaiah says woe to those who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left, and then they live alone in the land (Isaiah 5:8). Picture owning everything and having nobody to wave at from the porch. That's a whole lot of land for one set of footsteps, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD of Hosts says many houses will become desolate, and great mansions will be left unoccupied (Isaiah 5:9). Nobody is crowding in. Isaiah says he heard it himself, so he's passing it along just as he got it.

The answer is the grain. The LORD says a homer of seed will yield only an ephah of grain (Isaiah 5:10). That's the same bad news as the vineyard, just in the field. Plant a lot, get a little, friends.

The answer is the work of the LORD's hands. Isaiah says they disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see the work of His hands (Isaiah 5:12). The lyre, harp, tambourines, flutes and wine are all at their feasts. Those are the feasts where they miss it.

The answer is True. Isaiah says My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding (Isaiah 5:13). The word is understanding, and that's what's missing. I think that connects back to the feasts, where they didn't see the work of the LORD's hands (Isaiah 5:12).
The answer is Zion's nobles and masses. Isaiah says down go Zion's nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers (Isaiah 5:14). Nobles and masses are both named, friends. They go down together.

The answer is arrogant. Isaiah says mankind will be brought low, each man humbled, and the arrogant will lower their eyes (Isaiah 5:15). Heads that were held high end up looking at the ground. I think that's a hard way to learn to look down.

The answer is exalted. Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness (Isaiah 5:16). People get brought low, and He is lifted up. That's the contrast in the verse, bakers.

The answer is True. Isaiah says strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy (Isaiah 5:17). The verse also says lambs will graze as in their own pastures. Strangers are the ones feeding in what's left of the wealthy's places.

The answer is let Him hurry so we can see it. They say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it!” (Isaiah 5:19). Notice the verse before it is a woe for those who pull sin along with cart ropes (Isaiah 5:18). Those are the ones asking for the show to start, friends.

The answer is True. Isaiah says woe to those who call evil good and good evil (Isaiah 5:20). It sits right next to the darkness and light, and the bitter and sweet. It's all the same mix-up, friends. Everything gets the wrong label.

The answer is their own. Isaiah says woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight (Isaiah 5:21). The wisdom and the cleverness are in their own eyes. That's what this woe names.

The answer is the guilty. Isaiah says they acquit the guilty for a bribe (Isaiah 5:23). The same verse says they deprive the innocent of justice. When a bribe is involved, that's not justice, friends, that's a price tag.

The answer is False. Isaiah says they acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice (Isaiah 5:23). The innocent don't get what they should. It's the reverse of what a judge is supposed to do.

The answer is that they rejected the LORD's instruction. Isaiah says they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel (Isaiah 5:24). That's the reason he gives. The roots decay and the blossoms blow away like dust.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, “Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.” (Isaiah 5:25). It's a heavy line, friends. The anger is still burning and the hand is still upraised.

The answer is He whistles for them. Isaiah says He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth (Isaiah 5:26). No letter and no trumpet are in this verse. A banner goes up, a whistle goes out, and then Isaiah says, “Behold—how speedily and swiftly they come!”
The answer is False. Isaiah says no belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken (Isaiah 5:27). He adds that none of them grows weary or stumbles. No one slumbers or sleeps, either.

The answer is no one. Isaiah says they growl and seize their prey, and carry it away, and no one can rescue it (Isaiah 5:29). That's the picture of a lion at work. Once it's taken, nobody can get it back, friends.

The answer is darkness and distress. Isaiah says if one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress (Isaiah 5:30). It's a heavy picture, and I think it's meant to be. The very last thing in this passage is a dark sky.

The answer is True. Isaiah says even the light will be obscured by clouds (Isaiah 5:30). Darkness and distress are on the land, and even the light is dimmed. A heavy ending, friends, so I'll just let it sit.
